whatIsP2p.a: P2P Global — the Peer to Peer Global Discipleship Network — equips believers to grow in Christ. Everyone is learning from someone, and everyone is helping someone grow. It is rooted in Scripture, centered on Jesus, and for His glory.

whoBuilt.a: P2P Global Discipleship Network is powered by Amen Kingdom Tech Ministry — a technology ministry that designs and builds websites, apps, and digital systems for churches, organizations, and businesses.

whatIsAmen.q: What is Amen Kingdom Tech Ministry?
whatIsAmen.a: A purpose-driven technology ministry founded through obedience to God's calling in the digital age, existing to represent Him faithfully across the various mountains of influence in the tech world. The name AMEN reflects agreement with what God is doing through the systems it builds — guided by the Holy Spirit rather than trends alone, and built with excellence, precision, and integrity.

commercial.q: Is P2P a commercial product built by Amen Kingdom Tech?
commercial.a: No. P2P is a ministry expression of that same calling, not a business — which is exactly why every feature is free.

replaceChurch.q: Does P2P replace my local church?
replaceChurch.a: No. P2P is built to strengthen the local church, not compete with it. It does not replace pastors or legitimate church leadership. Membership, pastoral care and the sacraments stay where they belong — with your congregation.

therapyReplacement.q: Is P2P a replacement for therapy or professional counseling?
therapyReplacement.a: No. Where P2P touches care and wellness, it's peer encouragement alongside professional help, never a substitute for it. Anyone in crisis should reach out to a licensed professional or local emergency services.

giftsMarketplace.q: Is the Gifts & Service Network a marketplace where I pay for help?
giftsMarketplace.a: No. It is a vision for how believers can serve one another with their gifts — not a commercial marketplace, a freelancer platform or a paid services directory. Any gift-discovery feature would need safeguarding, privacy and moderation appropriate to what is offered.

whoCanJoin.a: Anyone who wants to grow as a disciple of Jesus and help someone else do the same — new believers and long-time believers alike. A peer guide is simply someone a little further along the road, not a distant authority.

cost.q: Is there a cost to join?
cost.a: No — P2P is free for individuals, families, churches, schools, organizations, communities, and other groups and institutions. There are no subscriptions, no premium memberships and no paywalls. This isn't a business model; it's a ministry, carried out in pursuit of God's vision that the earth would be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the Lord, as the waters cover the sea (Habakkuk 2:14).

whyFree.a: Because P2P exists to serve that vision, not to generate revenue from it. Charging for discipleship, prayer, or the tools to help someone grow would work against the very thing this network was built to do.

churchFree.q: Can my church use P2P for free too?
churchFree.a: Yes. Churches, schools, organizations, families and individuals all use the same free network — no paid tier, no premium plan, and nothing held back behind a paywall.

websiteVsApp.q: How is this website different from the P2P app?
websiteVsApp.a: This website helps you understand P2P — what it is, why it exists and how it works. The mobile app is where you experience it: Scripture, learning, relationships, prayer, families and churches. Where something described here is a direction rather than a current feature, the site says so.

peerGuide.a: A peer guide is a fellow believer who walks alongside you — sharing what they have learned, helping you understand and apply Scripture, and encouraging you to keep growing until you are able to guide someone else. A peer guide does not replace your pastor or your local church.

livingTree.a: The Living Tree visualises your discipleship development and the evidence behind it — your participation, learning, application and service. It is not a status symbol, a game, a spiritual ranking, or a measure of your worth.

growthStages.a: Dormant Seed, Sprout, Young Tree, Fruitful Tree, Forest Builder and Forest of Nations. A participant moves through them as evidence of participation, learning, application and service builds — not through time spent or attempts made. Forest of Nations is a vision-level outcome, not a claim that P2P has reached every nation.

grain.a: Grain is your harvest record. Every person who joins P2P Global through your personal invite link adds one Grain to your profile. Based on John 12:24 — a grain of wheat that falls into the earth and dies bears much fruit.

kingdomSchool.a: Kingdom School is P2P's structured discipleship learning. It begins with Core Foundations, which currently contains 188 published lessons across three courses — The Gospel & Salvation (84 lessons), The Christian Foundation (98 lessons) and Peer-to-Peer Orientation (6 lessons) — tracked from the start of a participant's growth journey, and learning continues beyond it, alongside Bible study, Kingdom Stories and other learning experiences.

languages.q: What languages is P2P available in?
languages.a: This website can be viewed in many languages, and translations are still being completed — where a page has not yet been translated, it is shown in English. The goal is that people can learn in the language they understand best.

generationalForest.a: The Generational Forest represents discipleship relationships and how they multiply across generations — the people who helped someone grow, and the people they in turn help. It is a picture of relationships, not a map of people or nations reached.

isAiTeacher.q: Does AI teach or evaluate people on P2P?
isAiTeacher.a: No. P2P does not position AI as a teacher, mentor, shepherd or spiritual evaluator. The model is people helping people grow — through Scripture, learning, relationships, application and service.

peerGuideChange.q: What happens if my peer guide changes?
peerGuideChange.a: Each participant has one active peer guide at a time for the main mentorship relationship, though a peer guide may walk with several people. Other people, pastors and shepherds may also contribute to your growth. Changing a peer guide does not reset your development.

evaluation.a: A participant completes the learning and its assessment, which is evaluated by qualified human peers. Assessment questions must be independently approved before the learning can count as assessed, and evaluation relates to that specific learning item. People who have completed and passed a particular item may qualify to evaluate that same item. Submitting an attempt is not an achievement, failed attempts are not presented as growth, and AI is not the evaluator.

bibleDeepStudy.q: Is the Bible part of Learning?
bibleDeepStudy.a: No — Bible is a primary experience with its own place in the app, separate from Learning, because Scripture is central to everything in P2P. It includes ordinary Scripture reading and supported Bible study. Deep Study is a separate experience within Bible Study for going further; it does not replace ordinary Bible reading.

p2pMail.a: P2P Mail is the official P2P inbox — its own area inside Messages, kept separate from your personal conversations. It is not an ordinary email account and does not replace external email services.

privacy.q: Can church leaders see my private reflections?
privacy.a: No. Private reflections remain private by default. Groups are private by default — only people who have been added or invited, and are authorized, can access them.

biblical-history.title: BIBLICAL HISTORY
biblical-history.body: The story Scripture tells — creation, the patriarchs, Israel, the kings, the prophets and the exile.
article: The Bible tells one unfolding story. It opens with God creating the heavens and the earth, and with humanity made in His image, then turns quickly to the reality of sin and its consequences. From Genesis 12 onward the story narrows to one man, Abraham, to whom God promised that through his offspring all the families of the earth would be blessed.

That promise runs through the history of Abraham's descendants: Isaac, Jacob and Joseph; Israel's slavery in Egypt and the Exodus under Moses; the covenant given at Sinai; the entry into Canaan; and the time of the judges. Israel's monarchy followed under Saul, David and Solomon, and God promised David a lasting kingdom.

After Solomon the kingdom divided. The prophets called Israel and Judah back to faithfulness and warned of judgment; the northern kingdom fell to Assyria, and later Jerusalem fell to Babylon. Yet the same prophets spoke of restoration and of a coming King, and after the exile a remnant returned to rebuild. The Old Testament closes still waiting for that promise to be fulfilled.

jesus-christ.title: JESUS CHRIST
jesus-christ.body: Who Jesus is, what He taught and did, His death and resurrection — the center of the whole story.
article: The four Gospels — Matthew, Mark, Luke and John — tell the story of Jesus of Nazareth, born in Bethlehem and raised in Galilee. They present Him as the fulfillment of the promises made to Abraham and David: the Messiah, the Son of God.

Jesus proclaimed that the kingdom of God had come near. He called disciples to follow Him, taught with authority, healed the sick and welcomed sinners — and He gave much of His ministry to investing in a small group of twelve, a pattern of discipleship that shaped everything that followed.

The Gospels give their longest attention to His final week: His entry into Jerusalem, His arrest, and His crucifixion under the Roman governor Pontius Pilate. On the third day, they testify, He rose from the dead and appeared to His followers, commissioning them to make disciples of all nations (Matthew 28:19–20). Christian faith stands on that testimony: Jesus Christ crucified, risen, and Lord.

early-church.title: EARLY CHURCH & APOSTLES
early-church.body: Pentecost, the apostles, and the spread of the Gospel recorded in Acts and the New Testament letters.
article: The book of Acts begins where the Gospels end. After Jesus' ascension, the Holy Spirit was poured out on His followers at Pentecost in Jerusalem; Peter preached, and about three thousand people were baptized (Acts 2). The first believers devoted themselves to the apostles' teaching, to fellowship, to the breaking of bread and to prayer.

Persecution scattered believers beyond Jerusalem, and the Gospel reached Samaria, an Ethiopian official, and the household of the Roman centurion Cornelius. The conversion of Saul of Tarsus — the apostle Paul — led to missionary journeys across Asia Minor and Greece, and churches were planted in cities such as Antioch, Philippi, Corinth and Ephesus.

The New Testament letters were written to many of these young churches — teaching sound doctrine, correcting error and encouraging faithful living. Paul's instruction to Timothy, to entrust what he had heard to faithful people who would teach others also (2 Timothy 2:2), captures the relational, generational pattern at the heart of P2P.

church-fathers.title: EARLY CHRISTIANITY & CHURCH FATHERS
church-fathers.body: The generations after the apostles, who guarded the faith, stated it carefully and handed it on.
article: The generations that followed the apostles are often called the early Church Fathers. Some — like Clement of Rome, Ignatius of Antioch and Polycarp of Smyrna — wrote letters around the turn of the second century that are still read today, encouraging churches to stay united and faithful under pressure.

In the second and third centuries, writers such as Justin Martyr, Irenaeus of Lyon and Tertullian explained and defended the faith against misunderstanding and false teaching. Irenaeus in particular stressed the continuity of the apostles' teaching, handed down through the churches.

After Christianity was legalized in the Roman Empire in the early fourth century, the Church met in councils to state its shared confession clearly. The Council of Nicaea in 325 affirmed that the Son is fully God — a confession Athanasius defended at great personal cost. These figures are studied not because they were without fault, but because they faithfully handed on what they had received.

christian-history.title: CHRISTIAN HISTORY
christian-history.body: The long story of the Church, from the early creeds to today.
article: The Church's story begins in the first century with a small band of disciples in Jerusalem, and the book of Acts records how the gospel spread rapidly along Roman trade routes through the missionary journeys of Paul and others, reaching most of the Mediterranean world within a few decades.

The early centuries were shaped by seasons of Roman persecution alongside the steady work of clarifying core Christian belief. Councils such as Nicaea (325) and Chalcedon (451) produced the creeds still recited in churches worldwide today, affirming the church's shared confession about who Jesus is.

In the centuries that followed, monastic communities preserved learning and Scripture through the medieval period, the Eastern and Western churches formally divided in 1054, and the Reformation of the 16th century — sparked by Martin Luther's 1517 challenge to the Church at Wittenberg — renewed the call to Scripture as the church's final authority. From there, the gospel continued to spread outward through the missionary movements of the following centuries, which is where the next category picks up.

revival.title: REVIVAL
revival.body: Seasons when God moved in unusual, widely-witnessed ways.
article: Church history includes recurring seasons where renewed conviction and prayer spread through whole communities faster than any single person organized. The First Great Awakening swept Britain and the American colonies in the 1730s–40s under preachers like George Whitefield and Jonathan Edwards, followed by a Second Great Awakening in the early 1800s.

The Welsh Revival of 1904–05, associated with a young evangelist named Evan Roberts, saw a wave of conversions and public prayer across Wales that was reported in newspapers of the day. Soon after, the Azusa Street Revival began in Los Angeles in 1906 under William J. Seymour, a meeting that historians widely credit as the origin point of the modern global Pentecostal movement.

Revivals like the East African Revival of the 1930s onward reshaped whole regional churches around confession, reconciliation, and renewed discipleship. What these seasons share isn't a formula — it's ordinary believers responding to an extraordinary sense that God was near, in ways that outlasted the moment itself.

global-church.title: GLOBAL CHURCH
global-church.body: How believers across cultures and continents live out the same faith.
article: One of the most significant shifts in modern church history has been geographic: researchers who track global Christianity — including the Center for the Study of Global Christianity and the Pew Research Center — have documented for decades how the church's center of gravity has moved away from Europe and North America toward Africa, Asia, and Latin America, where the fastest growth has occurred over the past century.

That means the 'typical' Christian today is less likely to be a European or North American than at almost any point since the early church, and more likely to worship in a language, style, and setting shaped by a very different culture than the ones that sent the first modern missionaries.

What holds this global, culturally diverse church together isn't uniformity — it's a shared confession about Jesus Christ, expressed through remarkably different languages, music, and forms of gathering. P2P's own peer-to-peer model reflects that same conviction: the faith travels through relationships, not through any one culture's ownership of it.

missions.title: MISSIONS
missions.body: Those sent to carry the gospel across cultures and borders.
article: Christian mission goes back to the New Testament itself, but the modern missionary movement is often dated to William Carey, an English cobbler-turned-missionary whose 1792 pamphlet and subsequent work in India helped launch a wave of Protestant missionary societies that would send workers across the globe through the 19th century.

Figures like Hudson Taylor, who founded the China Inland Mission in 1865 and pioneered missionaries adopting local dress and customs rather than imposing Western culture, shaped how later generations thought about crossing cultures with the gospel respectfully rather than as an extension of colonial power.

Today, one of the clearest trends in global missions is its reversal: churches in Africa, Asia, and Latin America — many of them planted by 19th- and 20th-century missionaries — now send significant numbers of their own missionaries worldwide, including back to the historically Christian West. Mission has become something the whole global church does together, in every direction.

people.title: PEOPLE
people.body: Figures whose faith shaped the Church that followed them.
article: Church history is carried forward by particular people whose lives are still studied today. Augustine of Hippo (354–430) shaped Western theology for over a thousand years after his conversion and his writing on grace, sin, and the nature of the church. Athanasius spent much of his life defending the Nicene understanding of Christ against fierce opposition, at real personal cost.

Francis of Assisi in the 13th century embodied simplicity and care for the poor in a way that still shapes how Christians think about possessions and creation. The Reformation produced Martin Luther and later John Calvin, while the 18th-century Wesleyan revival under John and Charles Wesley left behind not just hymns still sung today, but a whole model of small-group discipleship built around mutual accountability.

Missionary figures like Hudson Taylor and Amy Carmichael, who spent decades serving vulnerable children in India, remind us that faithfulness is usually measured in decades of unglamorous work, not single dramatic moments. None of these figures were without flaws — but their lives are part of the inheritance every believer today has received.

movements.title: MOVEMENTS
movements.body: Moments when discipleship multiplied faster than anyone expected.
article: Alongside individual figures, church history includes whole movements built around a particular way of forming disciples. Early monasticism, formalized by Benedict of Nursia's Rule in the 6th century, created communities organized around shared prayer, work, and Scripture that preserved the faith through unstable centuries.

The 18th-century Methodist movement under John Wesley organized converts into small 'class meetings' of a dozen or so people who met weekly for mutual accountability and encouragement in the faith — a structure historians credit with sustaining Methodism's rapid growth, and one that peer-to-peer discipleship models draw directly on today.

More recently, the house-church movement that sustained the Chinese church through decades of restriction, and the global spread of campus ministries and small-group or cell-church discipleship models, all share a common thread: faith multiplies fastest not through institutions alone, but through ordinary believers deliberately investing in a few others.

persecution.title: PERSECUTION & PERSEVERANCE
persecution.body: The cost some believers carry, and the faith that sustains them.
article: Persecution is part of the church's story from its earliest days — the book of Acts records the stoning of Stephen, widely regarded as the first Christian martyr, and Roman emperors including Nero and later Diocletian carried out organized persecutions in the first three centuries before Christianity was legalized in the empire.

The early church father Tertullian wrote that 'the blood of the martyrs is the seed of the church' — a pattern historians have observed repeat since: persecution has often coincided with growth rather than extinguishing the church it targeted.

Persecution of Christians continues in parts of the world today, and organizations such as Open Doors and Voice of the Martyrs document these situations in detail for anyone who wants to understand or pray specifically. We won't attach specific figures or claims here that we haven't verified — but we hold the reality in view, and it shapes how P2P thinks about prayer for the persecuted church as part of ordinary discipleship, not a separate concern.

christianity-today.title: CHRISTIANITY TODAY
christianity-today.body: What God is doing in the Church right now, told honestly.
article: Christianity remains the world's largest religion by number of adherents, and — as the Global Church category above touches on — its fastest-growing regions today are in the Global South rather than the historically Christian West, which is seeing continued secularization in many places even as immigration and renewal movements bring their own changes.

Digital tools have reshaped how many believers engage with Scripture, teaching, and community, for better and for worse — the same technology that lets a believer in one country study alongside a peer guide in another can also make faith feel like something consumed alone rather than lived in community. That tension is part of why P2P exists: to use technology in service of real relationships, not as a replacement for them.

None of this is a finished story. Whatever else is true of this moment in church history, ordinary discipleship — one person helping another follow Jesus — remains exactly as available and exactly as needed as it was in the first century.

continues.detail: The pattern continues, and the next generation of discipleship begins.

GrainPage.metaDescription: Your personal harvest record and how to invite others to Kingdom School.
GrainPage.heroTitle: A grain of wheat that falls into the earth.
GrainPage.heroSubtitle: Your personal record of who you've invited into this — and the fruit that follows.
GrainPage.prose1Body1: Every person who joins P2P Global through your personal invite link adds one Grain to your profile. It's based on John 12:24 — a grain of wheat that falls into the earth and dies bears much fruit. Grain isn't a leaderboard number or a currency you spend. It's a quiet, permanent record of who you brought into the journey with you.
GrainPage.prose1Body2: Your personal invite link lives in your profile. Share it with someone, and if they join, that's a Grain — a small, specific memory of one more person now walking this road.

ProfilePage.metaDescription: My Profile brings a participant's discipleship journey together — including their Living Tree, growth stage and milestones.
ProfilePage.heroSubtitle: A personal view of your growth — not a public performance.
ProfilePage.prose1Body: My Profile is one of the main areas of the app. It brings your discipleship journey together, including your Living Tree and the milestones that show how you are growing — what you have achieved, and what lies ahead.

tree.title: Your Living Tree
tree.body: A visual of your discipleship development and the evidence behind it.

stage.title: Your growth stage
stage.body: Where you are in the journey, from Dormant Seed onward — and why.

milestones.title: Milestones
milestones.body: What you have achieved, what remains, and how participation, learning, application and service each contribute.

PrayerPage.metaDescription: The Sinner's Prayer, prayer library, confession builder, and prayer journal inside P2P Global.
PrayerPage.heroTitle: Prayer, built into the app, not bolted on.
PrayerPage.heroSubtitle: Prayer as part of everyday discipleship — close at hand, not tucked away.
PrayerPage.prose1Body: Discipleship without prayer is just information. In the app, Prayer is found under More — close at hand alongside everything else, as part of everyday discipleship.

sinnersPrayer.title: The Sinner's Prayer
sinnersPrayer.body: A sacred screen — always accessible. A prayer of commitment for anyone who wants to begin with Jesus or recommit their life to Him. When you pray it — you can tell your peer guide immediately.

library.title: Prayer Library
library.body: Four categories — Grace and Mercy, Favour, Healing, and Confessions and Declarations. Biblical prayers grounded in Scripture, available any time.

confessionBuilder.title: Confession Builder
confessionBuilder.body: Build your personal daily confession. Select scriptures. Arrange them. Set a morning notification. Wake up to your own words of faith.

journal.title: Prayer Journal
journal.body: Write your prayers. Mark them answered. Your answered prayers become your personal testimony record — proof of God's faithfulness in your own life.

PeerGuidePage.metaDescription: What a peer guide is, how the peer-guide relationship works, and how every participant can become able to guide someone else.
PeerGuidePage.heroSubtitle: A fellow believer who shares what they have learned — and helps you become able to help someone else.
PeerGuidePage.prose1Body: Paul taught Timothy. Timothy was to entrust what he had received to faithful people, who would teach others also. The chain was relational, not institutional — and P2P exists to make that same pattern practical today.
PeerGuidePage.churchHeading: Not a replacement for pastoral leadership
PeerGuidePage.churchBody: The peer-guide relationship supports the local church. It does not replace pastors, shepherds or legitimate church leadership, and it never stands in for the care a local congregation gives.
PeerGuidePage.becomingHeading: What you receive, you pass on

PeerGuideExplainer.definition: A peer guide is a fellow participant who walks alongside another participant in their discipleship journey. Not a pastor, and not an authority over you — a peer who shares what they have learned.
whatTheyDo: Helps the other person understand and apply Scripture
Helps the participant become capable of guiding someone else

oneActive.title: One active peer guide
oneActive.body: Each participant has one active peer guide at a time, so the relationship stays clear.

multiple.title: A guide may walk with several
multiple.body: A peer guide may support more than one participant.

many.title: Others contribute too
many.body: Other people — including pastors and shepherds — may also contribute to a participant's development, while the main peer-guide relationship remains clear.

lasting.title: Development is never reset
lasting.body: Changing a peer guide does not reset a participant's development. Their growth and contribution history remain.

PeerGuideExplainer.becomingAGuide: The aim of every peer-guide relationship is that the participant becomes capable of guiding someone else. One person learns. One person grows. One person helps another grow. That person helps someone else grow. This is the pattern of 2 Timothy 2:2.

MessagingPage.metaDescription: Private conversations, private groups, family and church communication, calls, and the official P2P Mail inbox.
MessagingPage.heroSubtitle: Private conversations and relationships — built for walking with one another, not for a social feed.
MessagingPage.mailBody1: P2P Mail is the official internal communication area inside Messages. It is where official communication from P2P is received — kept separate from your personal conversations.
MessagingPage.mailBody2: P2P Mail is not an ordinary email account, and it is not a replacement for external email services.
MessagingPage.crisisBody: P2P is a peer discipleship network, not an emergency service. Anyone in immediate danger or crisis should contact local emergency services or a licensed professional directly.

direct.title: One-to-one messages
direct.body: Private conversations with the people you walk with, including your peer guide.

groups.title: Private groups
groups.body: Groups are private by default — only people who have been added or invited, and are authorized, can access them.

familyChurch.title: Family and Church
familyChurch.body: Communication for your Family Circle and your church community.

studyTogether.title: Study Together
studyTogether.body: Conversation connected to what you are learning together.

audio.title: Audio calls
audio.body: Talk with the people you are walking with.

video.title: Video calls
video.body: Meet face to face, wherever you are.

group.title: Group calls
group.body: Calls with several people, where available.

KingdomSchoolPage.metaDescription: How learning works in P2P: Kingdom School and Core Foundations (188 published lessons across 3 courses), Kingdom Stories, the Learning Centre and Study Together.
KingdomSchoolPage.heroSubtitle: Free, at your own pace, rooted in Scripture — and shared with others.
KingdomSchoolPage.prose1Heading: Many ways to learn. One direction.
KingdomSchoolPage.prose1Body: Learning in P2P is not limited to one course or one kind of content. The Learning area of the app brings several experiences together. The Bible is not one of them — it is a primary experience with its own place beside Learning. Everything points to the same goal: understanding Scripture and living it out.

kingdomSchool.title: Kingdom School
kingdomSchool.body: Structured discipleship learning. It begins with Core Foundations and continues with further Kingdom School learning.

stories.title: Kingdom Stories
stories.body: Learning the story of God's people — Biblical history, Jesus Christ, the early Church, Christian history and the spread of the Gospel.

learningCentre.title: Learning Centre
learningCentre.body: Where your learning is organized, so you can see what to do next and what is waiting for review.

studyTogether.title: Study Together
studyTogether.body: Studying alongside others, together with other supported learning experiences.

KingdomSchoolPage.foundationsHeading: 188 published lessons. Tracked from the beginning.
KingdomSchoolPage.foundationsBody1: Core Foundations is the core discipleship curriculum of Kingdom School. It currently contains 188 published lessons across three courses, and it is tracked from the very beginning of a participant's growth journey.
KingdomSchoolPage.foundationsBody2: Core Foundations is a foundation, not a finish line. People continue learning beyond it — through further Kingdom School learning, Bible reading and study, Kingdom Stories, learning plans and other learning experiences.
KingdomSchoolPage.workflowBody: The Learning Centre keeps learning organized around four simple states:

todo.title: To do
todo.body: Learning that is ready for you to work on.

submitted.title: Submitted
submitted.body: Work you have completed and handed in.

feedback.title: Feedback
feedback.body: Responses that help you understand and keep growing.

waiting.title: Waiting for review
waiting.body: Submissions that are still waiting to be reviewed.

evalPoints: A participant completes the relevant learning and its assessment.
Assessments are evaluated by qualified human peers.
Assessment questions must be independently approved before the learning can count as assessed.
Evaluation is based on the specific learning item.
People who have completed and passed a particular item may qualify to evaluate that same item.
Submitting an attempt is not an achievement, and failed attempts are never presented as growth.
AI is not the evaluator. People help people grow.

LivingTreePage.metaDescription: How growth is evidenced in P2P — participation, learning, application and service — and the stages from Dormant Seed to Forest of Nations.
LivingTreePage.heroSubtitle: A picture of discipleship development — not a status, a game, or a ranking.
LivingTreePage.prose1Heading: A visual of a real journey
LivingTreePage.prose1Body1: The Living Tree visualises a participant's discipleship development and the evidence of their participation, learning, application and service.
LivingTreePage.prose1Body2: It is not a status symbol, a game, a spiritual ranking, or a measure of a person's worth. Spiritual growth is not a competition. The tree helps a participant see where they are, what has contributed, and what lies ahead.
LivingTreePage.dimensionsBody: Growth is based on evidence — not merely on activity, and never on failed attempts.

participation.title: Participation
participation.body: Meaningful participation in the discipleship journey and in discipleship relationships.

learning.title: Learning
learning.body: Learning that has been completed and passed an approved assessment. Core Foundations currently contains 188 published lessons across three courses, and other recognized learning experiences also contribute to the wider learning journey.

application.title: Application
application.body: Distinct, verified practical actions that show learning is being applied. Application is cumulative — it is never reduced to minutes spent, forms submitted or activity volume.

service.title: Service
service.body: Approved, meaningful contributions. Duplicate or insignificant contributions are not counted as separate meaningful service.

LivingTreePage.milestonesBody: Rather than a single score, a participant's progress is explained through milestones:
milestones: What evidence contributed to the current stage.
Which milestones are needed to progress.
How participation, learning, application and service each contribute.
LivingTreePage.milestonesNote: The criteria are explained to participants in the app. Detailed internal thresholds are not published here.
LivingTreePage.treeHeading: The natural life of an apple tree
LivingTreePage.treeBody: The Living Tree draws on the real growth of an apple tree — from a germinating seed to a mature tree.
LivingTreePage.relationHeading: The tree's growth and a participant's growth are not identical
LivingTreePage.relationBody1: The visual development of the apple tree and a participant's growth matrix are related, but they are not the same system. The tree's biological stages describe how the image grows. The participant stages — Dormant Seed through Forest of Nations — describe discipleship development based on evidence.
LivingTreePage.relationBody2: A biological stage is not a promotion, and a participant stage is not a botanical description. The tree helps make growth visible; the evidence is what defines it.

seed.title: DORMANT SEED
seed.headline: The journey begins.
seed.body: Something has been planted. The participant has begun the discipleship journey, and the evidence of growth is still to come.

sprout.title: SPROUT
sprout.headline: Growth has begun.
sprout.body: The first evidence of growth is visible — participation in the journey, and learning that has started to take root.

youngTree.title: YOUNG TREE
youngTree.headline: Roots going deeper.
youngTree.body: Learning is building and being applied. Growth is becoming steady across more than one dimension.

fruitfulTree.title: FRUITFUL TREE
fruitfulTree.headline: Bearing fruit.
fruitfulTree.body: Learning is applied in daily life and shared in meaningful service. The fruit of discipleship is visible — not only for the participant, but through them.

forestBuilder.title: FOREST BUILDER
forestBuilder.headline: Helping others grow.
forestBuilder.body: The participant helps others grow, and discipleship begins to multiply through relationships — the pattern of 2 Timothy 2:2.

forestOfNations.title: FOREST OF NATIONS
forestOfNations.headline: The vision of Habakkuk 2:14.
forestOfNations.body: A vision-level outcome: discipleship multiplying across generations and nations until the earth is filled with the knowledge of the glory of the Lord. It is not a claim that P2P has already reached every nation.

GettingStartedPage.metaDescription: How the P2P journey begins — joining, walking with a peer guide, and starting Core Foundations.
GettingStartedPage.heroSubtitle: No deadline. No pressure. A clear picture of what happens first.
GettingStartedPage.proseHeading: The rhythm is yours to keep
GettingStartedPage.proseBody: From here the rhythm is simple: Scripture, learning, application and service, one step at a time, alongside your peer guide — until you are ready to help someone else grow.

KingdomStoriesPage.metaDescription: Kingdom Stories is a learning experience: Biblical history, Jesus Christ, the early Church, the Church Fathers, Christian history and the spread of the Gospel.
KingdomStoriesPage.heroTitle: Learning the Story of God's People
KingdomStoriesPage.heroSubtitle: Scripture, Biblical history, Jesus Christ, the early Church, and the continuing story of the Church.
KingdomStoriesPage.introHeading: More than inspirational audios and videos
KingdomStoriesPage.introBody1: Kingdom Stories is part of Learning in P2P. It helps people understand Scripture, Biblical history, Jesus Christ, the early Church, Christian history and the continuing story of the Church.
KingdomStoriesPage.introBody2: Understanding matters more than browsing. Reaching a category or opening a story does not, on its own, demonstrate learning — what matters is what is understood and carried into life.

areas.globalChurch: Christian History and the Global Church
areas.missions: Missions and the Spread of the Gospel

KingdomStoriesPage.moreHeading: More from the story of the Church
KingdomStoriesPage.prose1Body1: This is a growing library, not a source of fabricated statistics or unverified claims. Where a story is shared, we aim to represent it accurately and give proper context — Christian history deserves the same honesty we would want applied to our own.
KingdomStoriesPage.prose1Body2: Each overview here is a starting point, not the final word on its topic. Deeper learning on each area happens in Kingdom Stories inside the app.

PrivacyPage.heading: Privacy Policy
PrivacyPage.body: A full privacy policy will be published here before P2P collects any personal data through this website. Nothing on this site currently stores personal information beyond what your browser retains locally.

TermsPage.heading: Terms of Use
TermsPage.body: Full terms of use will be published here as P2P's features go live. This website is an informational site that explains the P2P Global Discipleship Network.

account.title: Join P2P
account.body: Download the app and create your account. Your journey begins from Home — your personal starting point in P2P.

peerGuide.title: Walk with a peer guide
peerGuide.body: Discipleship in P2P is relational. A peer guide walks alongside you as you learn — one active peer guide at a time.

foundations.title: Begin Core Foundations
foundations.body: Core Foundations is tracked from the very beginning of your growth journey. Learn at your own pace, complete each lesson and its assessment, and apply what you learn.

rhythm.title: Keep growing — and help someone else
rhythm.body: Read Scripture, keep learning, serve where you can. In time, you will be able to walk alongside someone else.

JoinPage.metaDescription: How to experience P2P Global in the app — current availability, and how the journey begins.
JoinPage.heading: Who Will You Help Grow?
JoinPage.storeNote: The Play Store listing isn't live yet — we'd rather leave this honest than link somewhere that doesn't exist.
JoinPage.freeNote: Free for individuals, families, churches, schools, organizations, communities, and other groups and institutions.

FaqPage.metaDescription: Answers to common questions about P2P — what it is, what it isn't, and how it relates to your church.

KingdomWinsPage.metaDescription: Look what God has done — a place for believers to share stories of His work in their lives.
KingdomWinsPage.heroSubtitle: A space for the community to share what He is doing — in words, pictures, and video.
KingdomWinsPage.prose1Heading: P2P is not the object of the story
KingdomWinsPage.prose1Body: When someone shares a Kingdom win, the point is never P2P's growth or reach. The story always points to Jesus — what He has done in a life, a family, or a community.
KingdomWinsPage.shapeBody: These are the kinds of stories this page will hold — categories, not claims. No specific wins are published yet.

prayer.title: ANSWERED PRAYER
prayer.outcome: God moving in a specific, named need.

life.title: A LIFE CHANGED
life.outcome: Someone coming to know Jesus, or growing in Him.

family.title: A FAMILY RESTORED
family.outcome: Reconciliation, healing, renewed hope at home.

group.title: A GROUP FORMED
group.outcome: Believers finding each other and starting to grow together.

church.title: A CHURCH STRENGTHENED
church.outcome: A local congregation encouraged or equipped.

sent.title: SOMEONE SENT
sent.outcome: A believer stepping into service or mission.

share.title: Share
share.body: A believer shares what God has done — in words, a photo, or a short video.

reviewed.title: Reviewed
reviewed.body: Shared honestly, with context, before it's published — no exaggeration, no fabrication.

pointsToHim.title: Points to Him
pointsToHim.body: Published in a way that gives glory to Jesus, not to P2P or to the person sharing.

KingdomWinsPage.prose2Body: This page will hold real testimonies from real people as the community grows. Until then, we won't fabricate stories, numbers, or partnerships just to make this page feel fuller than it is.

MissionsPage.metaDescription: See the field. Hear the story. Pray for the workers. Learn from the work. Go where God sends you.
MissionsPage.heroTitle: See the Mission. Hear the Story.
MissionsPage.heroSubtitle: Pray for the workers. Learn from the work. Go where God sends you.
MissionsPage.prose1Heading: P2P does not determine your calling
MissionsPage.prose1Body: Mission work belongs to God, carried out through the local church and the people He sends. P2P's role is simply to help believers see the field, learn well, pray specifically, and stay connected to what He is doing — never to decide someone's calling for them.
MissionsPage.prose2Body: A heart for missions isn't enough on its own — the workers who last are the ones who prepared well: in Scripture, in character, in cross-cultural humility, and in real accountability to a sending church. P2P's discipleship pathway exists partly to build that foundation before anyone goes.
MissionsPage.closingBody: Pray for the workers. Give as you're able. Go where He sends you.

field.title: FIELD
field.body: See where God is at work around the world.

story.title: STORY
story.body: Hear how He is moving, told honestly and without exaggeration.

scripture.title: SCRIPTURE
scripture.body: Ground every mission in the Word, not just in urgency.

prayer.title: PRAYER
prayer.body: Pray specifically for the workers, not just the need.

learning.title: LEARNING
learning.body: Learn what cross-cultural, faithful mission actually requires.

response.title: RESPONSE
response.body: Respond as God leads you — in prayer, giving, or going.

ChurchesPage.metaDescription: How P2P supports churches and their discipleship communities — free for every church.
ChurchesPage.heroSubtitle: P2P supports churches and their discipleship communities. It never replaces them.
ChurchesPage.prose1Body1: P2P is free for churches — and for individuals, families, churches, schools, organizations, communities, and other groups and institutions. No subscription, no paid tier, no feature held back behind a paywall. Small or large, house church or established congregation, every church is welcome.
ChurchesPage.prose1Body2: P2P exists to serve the local church, not to sell to it.
ChurchesPage.prose2Body1: Every pastor knows this question. Attendance can be counted. Discipleship is harder to see: whether people are being formed in the Word, whether new believers are walking with someone, and whether anyone is being equipped to help someone else grow.
ChurchesPage.prose2Body2: P2P helps a church cultivate discipleship relationships across its community — people helping people grow, under the care of the church's own leadership.
ChurchesPage.experienceHeading: What the church experience brings together

people.title: People and relationships
people.body: The church community, and the discipleship relationships within it.

shepherds.title: Shepherd and Co-Shepherd
shepherds.body: Roles that reflect the church's own leadership and its care for its people.

learning.title: Learning and curriculum
learning.body: Shared learning for the church community, including Kingdom School.

bible.title: Bible and study experiences
bible.body: Scripture reading and Bible study for the whole community.

prayer.title: Prayer
prayer.body: Praying for and with one another.

communication.title: Communication and calls
communication.body: Messages and calls for the church community.

media.title: Media
media.body: Media shared within the church community.

assignments.title: Assignments and reflections
assignments.body: Learning assignments, and space for personal reflection.

custom.title: Church-specific learning
custom.body: Custom learning content for a church's own context.

ChurchesPage.noteBody: This page describes the intended church experience. Specific leadership tools and permissions are explained inside the app as they become available.
ChurchesPage.privacyBody1: Private reflections remain private by default. P2P does not give church leaders access to the content of a person's private reflections.
ChurchesPage.privacyBody2: Groups are private by default — only people who have been added or invited, and are authorized, can access them.
ChurchesPage.ctaBody: Start by understanding how P2P works, then experience it in the app. It is free for every church.
ChurchesPage.heroImageAlt: A church steeple against a clear sky

FamiliesPage.metaDescription: The Family Circle supports shared discipleship and relationships within the family — gathering, learning, prayer and growing together.
FamiliesPage.heroSubtitle: Before it happens in a group or a curriculum, discipleship happens at the kitchen table.
FamiliesPage.prose1Heading: Family as the first discipleship context
FamiliesPage.prose1Body: Deuteronomy 6 puts the responsibility for passing on faith squarely in the home — talking about God's Word "when you sit in your house, when you walk by the way, when you lie down, and when you rise." P2P doesn't try to replace that. It supports it, through the Family Circle: a shared space for discipleship and relationships within the family.
FamiliesPage.prose2Body: None of this is meant to add pressure to already-full households. The aim is small, repeatable rhythms — a few minutes, a few times a week — not one more obligation competing for a family's time.

gather.title: GATHER
gather.body: Start a gathering, or join one — a simple way for the family to come together around Scripture, at the table, in the car or before bed.

learn.title: CONTINUE LEARNING
learn.body: Pick up learning together where you left off, so growth at home has continuity.

pray.title: PRAY TOGETHER
pray.body: Family prayer — naming what is hard, and thanking God for what is good.

connect.title: STAY CONNECTED
connect.body: Family chat and the people in your Family Circle, so relationships stay close through the week.

remember.title: REMEMBER THE JOURNEY
remember.body: History and highlights — looking back on what God has done in your family.

FamiliesPage.circleHeading: A shared space for the whole family
FamiliesPage.heroImageAlt: A family sitting close together at home

GiftsPage.metaDescription: The Body of Christ engine: how professional, creative, and ministry gifts can serve the Kingdom.
GiftsPage.heroSubtitle: Discipleship is not only receiving. It is also learning to give what God has placed in you.
GiftsPage.prose1Body1: A believer is not only a student of Scripture. They are a therapist, a developer, an administrator, an artist, a teacher, a worship leader — someone with real skills and real gifts that can strengthen the Kingdom, not just their own career.
GiftsPage.prose1Body2: What you learn can shape how you serve. What God has placed in you can strengthen someone else.
GiftsPage.prose2Body: This is deliberately not a place for influence, rankings, or "top contributor" badges. The only word that matters here is service. And where care touches sensitive areas — counseling, mental health, medical topics — professional qualifications and appropriate boundaries always matter; spiritual encouragement is not a substitute for professional treatment, and the two can coexist.
GiftsPage.heroImageAlt: Volunteers packing boxes of supplies together

DiscipleshipPage.metaDescription: The P2P discipleship model: peer learning, growth, guidance, and multiplication rooted in 2 Timothy 2:2.
DiscipleshipPage.heroSubtitle: Everyone is helping someone grow. That is the whole P2P model.
DiscipleshipPage.prose1Body1: Paul taught Timothy. Timothy was called to entrust what he'd received to faithful people, who would then teach others also. That is not a management hierarchy — it is a relational chain of faithfulness that Scripture assumes will keep going, generation after generation.
DiscipleshipPage.prose1Body2: P2P exists to make that pattern practical: Scripture, prayer, and community structured around real relationships, not passive content consumption.
DiscipleshipPage.prose2Body: In P2P, a "peer guide" is someone walking alongside you — not a titled authority standing over you, and not a replacement for your pastor. Guiding someone is simply sharing what you were taught, in relationship. Anyone who has grown can help someone else grow.
DiscipleshipPage.heroImageAlt: Hands resting on open Bibles as people study Scripture together

AboutPage.metaDescription: Why P2P exists, its theological foundation, and its relationship to Scripture and the local church.
AboutPage.heroSubtitle: Not a bigger platform. A faithful instrument for an ancient pattern.
AboutPage.prose1Body: P2P is not the hero of its own story. It does not replace Jesus Christ, Scripture, the Holy Spirit, the local church, or pastors and legitimate church leadership. It exists as one instrument among many that God can use to help believers learn, grow, walk with others, serve and multiply.
AboutPage.prose2Body: The name isn't incidental. P2P assumes that spiritual growth is relational and mutual — everyone is learning from someone, and everyone, no matter how new in the faith, has something to offer someone else. A guide is a further-along peer, not a distant authority.
AboutPage.prose3Heading: The Word has the final word
AboutPage.prose3Body: Every study plan, prompt, and piece of content in P2P is meant to point a person back to the Bible itself, not to stand in for it. Where anything here ever seems to add to or override what Scripture says, Scripture wins — P2P is a tool for engaging the text, never a substitute authority over it.
AboutPage.prose4Heading: A supporting instrument, not a substitute
AboutPage.prose4Body: P2P assumes every believer using it belongs, or is being pointed toward belonging, to a local church — with its own leadership, sacraments, and accountability. Nothing here is designed to be a person's only spiritual community. See how this plays out in practice on the <churches>Churches</churches> and <families>Families</families> pages.
AboutPage.prose5Body: Some of what is described across this site is the intended direction for P2P, not a claim that every part is already available. As P2P grows, this site will be updated to reflect what is real, and to label clearly what is still ahead.
AboutPage.prose6Body: P2P does not position AI as a teacher, mentor, shepherd or spiritual evaluator. Technology serves the relationships; it does not replace them.

VisionPage.metaDescription: For the earth will be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the Lord as the waters cover the sea. The vision behind P2P.
VisionPage.heroTitle: The Earth Filled With His Glory
VisionPage.heroSubtitle: Habakkuk 2:14 is not a slogan for P2P — it is the horizon everything here is aimed at.
VisionPage.prose1Heading: A vision bigger than a platform
VisionPage.prose1Body1: P2P is not ultimately about building a bigger platform, a larger user base, or a more impressive product. It is about participating — in a small, ordinary, faithful way — in the spread of the knowledge of the glory of the Lord across every city and nation.
VisionPage.prose1Body2: That means the measure of success is never the network itself. It is whether people are actually coming to know Jesus Christ more deeply, and helping someone else do the same.
VisionPage.prose2Body: P2P is an instrument — a set of tools and relationships that help believers learn, grow, walk with others, serve, disciple, and multiply. It is not a replacement for Jesus, for Scripture, for the Holy Spirit, or for the local church. Where this vision succeeds, the glory belongs to Him, not to a platform.
VisionPage.heroImageAlt: The sun rising over a calm sea

HowItWorksPage.metaDescription: How P2P Global works — peer-to-peer discipleship, learning, the Bible, the Living Tree, peer guides, families, churches and the P2P app.
HowItWorksPage.heroSubtitle: From your first step to helping someone else grow.
HowItWorksPage.proseHeading: This website explains. The app is where you take part.
HowItWorksPage.proseBody: Each part of P2P is explained here in plain language, so that when you open the app you already understand what you are walking into. Read what is relevant to you — or read everything.

LearningJourney.heading: Rooted in Scripture. Learned together.
LearningJourney.body: Learning in P2P is not a single course or a content library. It brings together Bible reading, structured discipleship, the story of the Church and shared study — always pointing back to Scripture itself.

bible.title: The Bible
bible.body: Bible is a primary experience in the app, separate from Learning — ordinary Scripture reading, supported Bible study, and Deep Study for going further.

kingdomSchool.title: Kingdom School
kingdomSchool.body: Structured discipleship learning, beginning with Core Foundations — currently 188 published lessons across three courses, tracked from the very start of the journey — and continuing beyond it.

stories.title: Kingdom Stories
stories.body: Learning the story of God's people — from Biblical history and the life of Jesus to the early Church, Christian history and the spread of the Gospel.

studyTogether.title: Study Together
studyTogether.body: Learning alongside others, so understanding is shared, questioned and applied — not just consumed alone.

AppExperience.eyebrow: Understand here. Experience in the app.
AppExperience.heading: Where P2P is lived
AppExperience.body: This website explains P2P. The mobile app is where people actually take part — in Scripture, learning, relationships, prayer, families and churches. These are its main experiences:

home.title: Home
home.body: A personal starting point — continue your discipleship journey, see what is relevant now, and reach the important parts of P2P.

learning.title: Learning
learning.body: The central learning environment: Kingdom School, Kingdom Stories, the Learning Centre, Study Together and other supported learning experiences.

bible.title: Bible
bible.body: Scripture has its own place, separate from Learning — ordinary Bible reading and supported Bible study, including Deep Study.

messages.title: Messages

BiblePage.metaDescription: Bible reading is a core part of P2P, with its own place in the app — and Deep Study offers a distinct experience for studying Scripture further.
BiblePage.heroSubtitle: Bible reading is a core part of P2P — so it has its own place in the app, not hidden inside Learning.
BiblePage.prose1Heading: Scripture is not one feature among many
BiblePage.prose1Body: Every part of P2P is meant to point people back to the Bible itself. That is why Bible remains a primary destination in the app, separate from the general Learning area.
BiblePage.featuresHeading: What the Bible experience is designed around

text.title: Bible text
text.body: Read Scripture itself, chapter by chapter.

audio.title: Audio Bible
audio.body: Listening to Scripture, where licensed audio recordings have been implemented.

translations.title: Translation selection
translations.body: Choosing a Bible translation, from those the app is licensed to offer.

navigation.title: Chapter and verse navigation
navigation.body: Move directly to the passage you are looking for.

compare.title: Comparing translations
compare.body: Reading a passage in more than one available translation.

deeper.title: Deeper study
deeper.body: A path from reading into closer study of the text.

BiblePage.deepHeading: A distinct space for going deeper
BiblePage.deepBody1: Deep Study is a separate experience within Bible Study. It is distinct from ordinary Bible reading — for the times you want to slow down and study a passage more closely.
BiblePage.deepBody2: Deep Study does not replace ordinary Bible reading. Reading Scripture regularly, simply and prayerfully remains at the heart of the journey.
BiblePage.availabilityNote: Specific Bible translations, versions and audio recordings appear in the app only where they have been implemented and their licensing permits it. This website does not list particular versions.

youngRoots.body: Fine roots begin drawing in water and nutrients.

matureTree.title: Mature tree
matureTree.body: A mature tree bears fruit season after season, carrying seed for what comes next.

StudyTogetherPage.metaDescription: Study Together is a shared learning experience that supports Kingdom School, Bible Study, Kingdom Stories and the wider learning journey.
StudyTogetherPage.heroSubtitle: A shared learning experience that can support every part of the learning journey.
StudyTogetherPage.prose1Body1: Study Together lets people learn alongside one another — reading, discussing, asking questions and applying what they learn together. It can support the different learning areas in P2P: Kingdom School, Bible Study, Kingdom Stories and more.
StudyTogetherPage.prose1Body2: Study Together has its own communication inside P2P, so conversation stays connected to what is being learned.
StudyTogetherPage.supportsHeading: One way of learning, many areas

kingdomSchool.title: Kingdom School
kingdomSchool.body: Working through Kingdom School learning together.

bible.title: Bible Study
bible.body: Studying a passage of Scripture together.

stories.title: Kingdom Stories
stories.body: Learning the story of the Church together.

community.title: Families and churches
community.body: Learning together as a family or a church community.

StudyTogetherPage.privateBody: Groups are private by default — only people who have been added or invited, and are authorized, can access them. Studying together never changes how a person's own learning is evaluated — each learning item is still evaluated on its own.
